title: Small grants
amount_raw: generally fall in a range of £1,500-£5,000; will only exceptionally exceed £6,000 (travel: up to £2,000/£2,500 per person; up to £5,000 for PhD fieldwork of 6+ months)
eligibility_summary:
Applicants must belong to, or provide evidence of support from, an organisation or institution willing to receive grant funds; individuals seeking support for personal projects not accepted, though UK office may consider individuals with organisational backing. Does not support undergraduate or master's students; grant payments cannot be made to personal bank accounts. UK-originating projects apply to the UK office.

Grant money can be used to support activities such as:

Festivals, workshops, performances and other events that present aspects of Japan to the UK or the UK to Japan in cultural, scientific, social, sporting and other spheres.
Exchanges between the two countries that enable participation and interaction, for instance of schools and sporting groups, artists, artisans, performers, scientists and researchers.
Collaborative projects involving UK and Japanese participants that result in new and innovative outputs for public, academic or professional presentation.
The teaching and development of Japanese language and cultural studies in schools, and higher education.
Academic research, visits and exchange, where these push forward the boundaries of knowledge and understanding or involve collaboration and co-production.
summary: Seed-funding small grants for projects bringing the UK and Japan together to deepen mutual understanding, exchange ideas/expertise or build collaboration; any field including arts and culture, humanities, Japanese language, medicine and health, science, youth and education, and sport. UK office runs three award rounds a year.
discipline_tags: arts and culture;humanities;social issues;Japanese language;medicine and health;science;youth and education;sport
notes: Recurring scheme with three annual UK-office deadlines: 31 March (decision May), 15 September (decision Nov), 15 December (decision March). Page gives NO YEARS; deadlines inferred for the snapshot year 2026 (31 Mar 2026 already past on 2026-08-21, so listed 15 Sep 2026 and 15 Dec 2026) - FLAG FOR REVIEW: year inference. status=open: applications continuously accepted across recurring rounds. Japan office has separate deadlines (28 Feb, 30 Sep) for Japan-based orgs - noted, not a separate row. amount not a clean min/max (case-by-case, no formal limit except PhD/travel caps); £1,500-£5,000 usual range, £6,000 exceptional cap used as max - amount bounds uncertain. Japan office PhD travel awards up to Y300,000 (yen, not GBP). Canonical own page; also listed on /grants/ index.

title: Butterfield Awards in medicine and health
amount_raw: up to £10,000 (continuing projects up to 3 years, max £10,000 per year, total limit £30,000)
eligibility_summary: Applicants should normally show an existing research record; consideration also given to practitioners, managers, carers or others in health-related fields intending to establish working links or produce a publishable comparative study. Project must involve partners in both the UK and Japan and be supported by two referees from different institutions to the project partners. Apply to the UK office regardless of where based. Preference to those new to UK-Japan collaboration and early-career applicants.
summary: Annual awards of up to £10,000 supporting exchanges and collaborations between health and medical professionals in Japan and the UK, including study of scientific, clinical, social and economic issues in healthcare; up to 3-year continuing projects to £30,000 total.
